overview: Indonesia is the world's largest country made up entirely of islands, with more than 17,000 islands between the Indian and Pacific oceans. Its capital is Jakarta, although a new capital, Nusantara, is being built on the island of Borneo. Indonesia declared independence from the Netherlands in 1945. It has the largest Muslim population of any country.

geography.text: Indonesia stretches more than 5,000 kilometres from east to west. Its largest islands include Sumatra, Java, Sulawesi, and parts of Borneo and New Guinea, which it shares with its neighbours. It lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has more active volcanoes than any other country. Java is one of the most densely populated islands on Earth, and much of the country is covered by tropical rainforest.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical and humid, with a wet and a dry season.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Orangutans, Komodo dragons, Sumatran tigers and birds of paradise.

history.text: Indonesia's islands were home to powerful kingdoms such as Srivijaya and Majapahit, which grew rich from trade. The Dutch gradually took control from the 1600s. Indonesia declared independence in 1945 and fought the Dutch until 1949. Suharto ruled from 1967 until 1998, when Indonesia became a democracy.

events.title: Borobudur
events.text: The giant Buddhist temple of Borobudur is built on Java.

events.title: Majapahit
events.text: The Majapahit Empire is founded on Java.

events.title: Dutch East India Company
events.text: The Dutch begin taking control of the spice trade.

events.title: Independence declared
events.text: Sukarno declares independence; the Dutch recognise it in 1949.

events.title: Suharto falls
events.text: Protests end 31 years of rule and open the way to democracy.

events.title: Tsunami
events.text: An earthquake and tsunami kill about 170,000 people in Aceh.

government.text: Indonesia is a presidential republic and the world's third-largest democracy. The President is elected directly for up to two five-year terms. The People's Consultative Assembly includes the elected House of Representatives. Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara, on the island of Borneo.

economy.text: Indonesia has the largest economy in South-East Asia. It is the world's biggest producer of palm oil and nickel, which is used in electric vehicle batteries, and a big exporter of coal. Manufacturing, tourism, especially to Bali, and a fast-growing digital economy are also important.

culture.text: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands and hundreds of ethnic groups and languages, united by Bahasa Indonesia. It has the largest Muslim population in the world, while Bali is mostly Hindu. Batik, wayang shadow puppets and gamelan music are all listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Borobudur
items.text: The world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 800s.

items.title: Batik
items.text: Cloth decorated using wax and dye, listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Nasi goreng, fried rice, and rendang, slow-cooked spicy beef.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Gamelan orchestras, wayang shadow puppets and batik cloth, all listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On Nyepi, the Balinese day of silence, the whole island stops: no lights, travel or noise.

sport.text: Badminton is Indonesia's most successful sport, with Olympic golds since 1992. Football is the most popular sport to watch, and pencak silat, a martial art, is national heritage.

items.title: Badminton
items.text: Indonesia's first Olympic gold came in badminton in 1992.

items.title: Pencak silat
items.text: A martial art listed by UNESCO.
Jakarta and Palembang hosted the Asian Games.

didYouKnow: Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, live only in Indonesia.

keyPeople.name: Raden Ajeng Kartini
keyPeople.text: Fought for girls' education in the 1890s.

keyPeople.name: Susi Susanti
keyPeople.text: Won Indonesia's first Olympic gold, in 1992.
